2026 Blue Element Freediving Competition: Results, World Records and Highlights

The 2026 Blue Element Freediving Competition, held November 8–17 in Soufrière Bay, Dominica, delivered two historic freediving world record performances, multiple national records and exceptional dives from some of the world's most accomplished freedivers.

Ukrainian freediver Kateryna Sadurska became the first woman to reach 90 meters in Constant Weight No Fins (CNF), while fellow Ukrainian athlete Nataliia Zharkova established a new women's Constant Weight (CWT) benchmark of 124 meters using a monofin.

Both performances surpassed the previous deepest competition dives recognized across AIDA and CMAS, further pushing the boundaries of human underwater performance.

Kateryna Sadurska: 90-Meter CNF Freediving World Record

On November 11, 2026, Ukrainian freediver Kateryna Sadurska made history by successfully completing a 90-meter Constant Weight No Fins (CNF) dive in 3 minutes and 33 seconds.

The performance made Sadurska the first woman in competitive freediving history to reach 90 meters without fins.

Constant Weight No Fins is widely considered one of the most technically and physically demanding disciplines in competitive freediving. Athletes descend and ascend using only their own swimming movements, without fins or assistance from the dive line for propulsion.

Sadurska's performance surpassed her previous AIDA world record of 86 meters and her CMAS benchmark of 88 meters, established in Dominica in November 2025.

Record dive details:

Athlete: Kateryna Sadurska

A former Olympic artistic swimmer, Sadurska has become one of the most accomplished no-fins freedivers in the history of the sport.

Nataliia Zharkova: 124-Meter CWT Freediving World Record

On November 14, 2026, Ukrainian freediver Nataliia Zharkova completed a 124-meter Constant Weight (CWT) dive, surpassing the previous women's monofin depth benchmark of 123 meters.

The performance marked Zharkova's first world record in the Constant Weight discipline and represented another major milestone in her international competitive freediving career.

Constant Weight freediving requires athletes to descend and ascend under their own power while maintaining the same ballast throughout the dive. Competitive athletes typically use a monofin to maximize propulsion and hydrodynamic efficiency.

Athlete: Nataliia Zharkova (also listed as Natalia Zharkova)

Zharkova's performance reinforced Ukraine's position among the leading nations in international women's competitive freediving.

Final-Day World Record Attempts

The final competition day, November 17, featured additional world record attempts from both Ukrainian record breakers.

Nataliia Zharkova announced a 127-meter CWT dive, reaching the announced depth but receiving a disqualification.

Kateryna Sadurska attempted a 91-meter CNF dive but turned early at 32 meters.

Neither attempt superseded the successful world record performances established earlier in the competition.

Understanding Competitive Depth Freediving Disciplines

The 2026 Blue Element competition included four internationally recognized depth freediving disciplines.

Abbreviation

Discipline

Description

CWT

Constant Weight

Divers descend and ascend using fins, commonly a monofin.

CWTB

Constant Weight Bifins

Divers use two separate fins for propulsion.

CNF

Constant Weight No Fins

Divers swim to depth and back without fins.

FIM

Free Immersion

Divers use the dive line to pull themselves down and back to the surface.

All four disciplines require exceptional breath-hold capacity, equalization skills, physical conditioning and mental preparation.

Why Dominica Is a World-Class Freediving Destination

Soufrière Bay, located on the southwestern coast of Dominica, has become an internationally recognized destination for competitive depth freediving.

The protected bay provides favorable training and competition conditions, including:

Deep water close to shore

Warm Caribbean water

Generally favorable currents and surface conditions

Established freediving training infrastructure

Experienced international safety and competition teams

Founded in 2015, Blue Element has helped establish Dominica as a premier destination for competitive freediving, attracting world record holders, professional athletes and recreational freedivers.
